capabilities.name: define-positioning
capabilities.description: Author a positioning document the studio commits will hold under twelve months of market pressure: who the client is, against whom, with what proof points.
capabilities.input: prospect brief, audience synthesis, competitive synthesis
capabilities.output: positioning brief signed by Marco, structured to feed downstream capabilities
capabilities.slo_targets: holds 12 months under market pressure (measured at 12-month follow-up); brief delivered within 3 weeks of accepted engagement
capabilities.invocation_modality: structured request via pitch flow → kickoff workshop; runs once per engagement
capabilities.moat_rationale: Marco signs every positioning brief; the document goes out under his name on every engagement. The skill is years of pattern-recognition not transferable in a handover.

capabilities.name: define-visual-language
capabilities.description: Define the visual language for an engagement on top of the positioning brief: typography, colour, imagery direction, motion principles.
capabilities.output: visual language specification (typography, colour, motion, imagery direction)
capabilities.slo_targets: coherent with positioning (Lena's signoff); delivered within 4 weeks of positioning brief
capabilities.invocation_modality: structured request following positioning brief sign-off
capabilities.moat_rationale: Lena signs the visual language; the studio's visual identity carries her judgement. Not transferable in a handover.

capabilities.name: author-brand-book
capabilities.description: Build the brand book as a single coherent artefact, the studio's most-recognized output. Personally integrated by the design lead.
capabilities.input: positioning brief, visual language specification, identity system
capabilities.slo_targets: integrated by Lena; delivered within 6 weeks of identity system handoff
capabilities.invocation_modality: structured request following identity system completion
capabilities.moat_rationale: Lena integrates the chapters into one coherent volume; the brand book is the studio's signature deliverable. Mid-level designers may produce chapters under her review, but the integration stays with her.

capabilities.name: build-identity-system
capabilities.description: Build the full identity system: typography, colour, grid, motion, illustration direction.
capabilities.slo_targets: complete coverage of declared touchpoints; delivered within 4 weeks of visual language sign-off
capabilities.invocation_modality: structured request following visual language sign-off; senior designers under Lena's review
capabilities.moat_rationale: Standard practice every studio in the category executes. Differentiation lives in the visual language above this, not in the system itself.

capabilities.name: design-ui
capabilities.description: UI design for B2B web and apps: screens, components, prototyping, accessibility.
capabilities.output: UI screens ready for engineering handoff
capabilities.slo_targets: WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility; delivered iteratively in 2-week sprints
capabilities.invocation_modality: structured request post-identity-system; senior product designer leads, product lead reviews
capabilities.moat_rationale: AI levels the field on UI production fast. Standard practice the studio shares with the category.

capabilities.name: document-design-system
capabilities.description: Document a design system handed off to clients who maintain their own product engineering long-term.
capabilities.output: design system documentation a client team can maintain
capabilities.slo_targets: covers components used in deliverables; client onboarding completed within 2 weeks of handover
capabilities.invocation_modality: structured request post-UI completion; mid-level product designers under senior lead
capabilities.moat_rationale: Standard component-library work; clients can also commission this from larger product agencies.

capabilities.name: hand-off-engagement
capabilities.description: Run the closeout ritual at the end of each engagement: every deliverable archived, every sign-off logged.
capabilities.input: all engagement deliverables (brand book, identity system, design system, UI screens)
capabilities.slo_targets: every deliverable archived and signed; closeout meeting within 2 weeks of final delivery
capabilities.invocation_modality: structured ritual at engagement close; Tomás runs it with discipline lead present
capabilities.moat_rationale: Coordination practice; required to close engagements cleanly but not differentiating in the market.

capabilities.name: synthesize-audience
capabilities.description: Synthesize the audience for an engagement: who the brand serves, what they say, what they buy, what they leave.
capabilities.input: prospect brief, market access (interviews, panels, public data)
capabilities.output: audience synthesis used as input for define-positioning
capabilities.slo_targets: synthesis sourced from at least 3 distinct signal types; delivered within 2 weeks of brief acceptance
capabilities.regulatory_constraints: GDPR if the synthesis touches identifiable user data
capabilities.invocation_modality: structured request at engagement open; strategy team executes
capabilities.moat_rationale: Standard research practice the studio executes competently. AI assists synthesis once the structure is in place.

capabilities.name: synthesize-competitive
capabilities.description: Synthesize the competitive landscape: who plays in the prospect's category, with what positioning, how each is moving.
capabilities.output: structured competitive synthesis used as input for define-positioning
capabilities.slo_targets: covers at least 5 competitors with positioning angles named; delivered within 2 weeks of brief acceptance
capabilities.invocation_modality: structured request at engagement open; strategy team executes
capabilities.moat_rationale: Standard competitive-audit practice. AI accelerates the data gathering once the synthesis frame is in place.

current_human_compositions.trigger: A returning client asks for a brand refresh 18 months later
current_human_compositions.description: The studio runs the same flow it would for a new client; the prior engagement is in delivered files but not retrievable in a useful way.
current_human_compositions.failure_modes: Marco and Lena pull from memory of the past engagement; insights from the prior brief don't compound into the new one. Effectively the second engagement starts from zero.

current_human_compositions.trigger: Tomás's weekly check-in note mentions scope drift
current_human_compositions.description: Marco reviews every weekly check-in note Tomás writes and decides whether to escalate to a scope-renegotiation conversation. Three engagements in 2025 needed his intervention. No formal capability is composed; the work is entirely human-mediated.
current_human_compositions.failure_modes: Founder is in the loop on every drift signal across 14 engagements per year; the bottleneck scales with engagement count.

current_human_compositions.description: Marco, Lena and Tomás each pull from their own memory of past clients to compose a positioning angle for the pitch.
current_human_compositions.failure_modes: Lessons from past engagements don't surface unless the pitch happens to remind one of the three of a relevant case. Pattern is fragile and doesn't compound.

potential_compositions.trigger: A returning client asks for a brand refresh
potential_compositions.description: Prior engagement loads into the kickoff: positioning, visual language, brand book, what was learned about the client's market. The kickoff becomes a shorter and more strategic conversation.
potential_compositions.precondition: A context-keeping practice exists that captures each engagement in a queryable shape, owned by a named role.

potential_compositions.trigger: A check-in note hints at scope drift
potential_compositions.description: Pattern-match across past drift episodes flags the early-warning signal automatically; Tomás escalates without Marco being in the loop on every case.
potential_compositions.precondition: The studio has captured what scope drift looks like across 30+ engagements and the patterns are queryable.

interfaces.name: Pitch meeting
interfaces.description: Where a prospect first sees the studio's work and gets a price.
interfaces.today_state: Delivers proposal and price. Captures the prospect's stated brief but no structured trace of which positioning angles were tried, why this prospect chose the studio, what objections came up.
interfaces.signals_lost_today: Stated objections, comparison set the prospect was running, what made them choose Outline. All three live in Tomás's and Marco's recall.
interfaces.after_state_hint: The pitch becomes a structured signal: brief on the way in, chosen angle and objections logged on the way out. Feeds the per-caller world model.

interfaces.name: Kickoff workshop
interfaces.description: The engagement opens with a 1-day workshop: scope, calendar, single point of contact, deliverables agreed.
interfaces.today_state: Delivers shared understanding for the team and the client. Captures scope and calendar in a SOW; transcript and decisions live as Tomás's notes plus what people remember.
interfaces.signals_lost_today: Live client reactions, the questions they don't yet know to ask, the assumptions they bring. None of these are captured in a queryable form.
interfaces.after_state_hint: Workshop transcript indexed, decisions captured as structured signal, prior-engagement context loaded for returning clients via read-engagement-memory.

interfaces.name: Weekly check-in call
interfaces.description: Recurring 30-min call on every active engagement: progress, blockers, next-week scope.
interfaces.today_state: Delivers a status update and unblocks decisions. Tomás writes a note Marco reads to decide on escalations. The note exists; structured signal does not.
interfaces.signals_lost_today: Drift signals (today only Marco notices), client pace changes, scope-creep early indicators. All three pass through unrecorded.
interfaces.after_state_hint: Notes pattern-matched against past drift episodes via recognize-scope-drift; Tomás escalates without Marco needing to read every note.

interfaces.name: Asset handover meeting
interfaces.description: Closing meeting where the client receives every artefact and signs off.
interfaces.today_state: Delivers the artefacts. Captures sign-off in a signed log.
interfaces.signals_lost_today: What the client expects from the artefacts in the next 12 months, which decisions they will revisit, what they will defer. Lost as soon as the meeting ends.
interfaces.after_state_hint: Handover captures the client's stated forward-looking expectations; feeds into a 12-month follow-up loop (run-12-month-followup) that closes the cycle.

decisions.question: What does this studio actually own that nobody else does?
decisions.answer:
The studio owns four things that are hard to copy: the way Marco writes a positioning document, the way Lena defines a visual language, the way Lena builds a brand book, and the strategy → identity → digital-product flow run as one engagement. Everything else — kickoff workshops, weekly check-ins, asset handover, UI design, design-system documentation — is competent practice the studio shares with every other shop in the category.

The studio sells one fixed price for both. The four things make the price; the rest fills the engagement. Naming this distinction at pitch is the first move.

decisions.question: What is held together by people today that could be held together by a system?
decisions.answer:
Three places where the studio pays the alignment cost in meeting hours: (1) a returning client comes back 18 months later for a refresh — the prior engagement is in delivered files but not retrievable, so the second engagement starts from zero; (2) scope-drift detection — Tomás's weekly check-in notes get reviewed by Marco who decides whether to escalate, on every engagement; (3) the pitch — Marco, Lena and Tomás each pull from their own memory of past clients to compose a positioning angle.

All three would compound if the studio kept what it learned about each client in a queryable shape. The next hire is the role that owns that shared memory and lets it accumulate across engagements.

decisions.question: Which piece does the structure suggest building next?
decisions.answer:
The map names three places where the response would be put together by hand today because a needed function isn't there yet: a returning-client context retrieval, a scope-drift early-warning, and a post-handover market check-in 12 months after delivery. None of these are exotic. Each one shares the same missing capability: a context-keeping practice that captures past engagements as something the next engagement can read.

Build that one capability and three of these gaps close at once. The ROI is not in the artefact — it's in the compounding effect on every engagement after.
